messages:
Maya: FYI i'm spinning up the horizon14b (int4) canary on dedicated pool — quick eval pass shows a perf / quality oddity, and a couple OOMs on longer seqs :eyes:
Sam: saw that earlier in the log dump, looks like KV growth + fragmentation. pasted error from node-3:
```
  runtime: out of memory: failed to allocate 3.2 GiB for KV cache (device 0)
  at Serve::alloc_kv_cache() +0x12f
  kv_cache_used=14.1GiB kv_cache_capacity=15.9GiB
```
Sam: OOM happens after sustained 900-1200 token generations with windowed batching enabled, batch_size=8
Jordan: hypothesis: int4 reduces memory for weights but increases activation pressure + causes more frequent KV allocations (we've seen internal fragmentation). quick tests to run:
- reduce default max_new_tokens from 1024 -> 512 for horizon14b int4 canary
- enable kv_compaction_interval=200 (compacts free slots every N steps)
- lower batch_size to 4 for canary
Reeva: adding eval plan — we should run: 
1) eval-harness --model horizon14b --quant int4 --seed 42 --max_new_tokens 512 --batch 4 --suites codebench,dialog-bench
2) eval-harness same with int8 and float16 baselines
3) run long-seq stress: regen 2x samples with length 1400 to reproduce OOM
Command (copy): `./tools/eval_harness.sh --model horizon14b --quant int4 --suites codebench,dialog-bench --max_new_tokens 512 --batch 4`
Maya: ran the 512/batch4 sweep overnight — quick summary:
- codebench BLEU: float16 31.8 -> int4 29.7 (-2.1)
- dialog-bench emscore: 0.63 -> 0.57 (-0.06)
- perplexity up ~12% vs float16
- OOMs: went from 3 events -> 0 with kv_compaction_interval=200 and batch_size=4 :thumbsup:
Sam: good signal. can you paste the exact canary config you deployed?
Maya: config snippet:
```
model: horizon14b
quant: int4
max_new_tokens: 512
batch_size: 4
kv_compaction_interval: 200
batching: windowed
```
Jordan: quality regression magnitude looks consistent with coarser quantization in some code generation patterns. action items:
- run targeted quantization ablation: per_channel vs per_tensor, quant_noise 0.02, calibrate with 2k samples
- run eval with temperature=0.8 and 0.2 to check hallucination sensitivity
- measure token latency p50/p95 under batch=4 vs 8 (shouldn't regress too much)
Reeva: i'll queue up the per_channel vs per_tensor sweep today, also will run a tiny calibration set to check weight outliers. will report by EOD.
infra-bot: canary deployment 2471239999 started for pool-dedicated-8xA100 (maya).
Sam: proposing a short-term mitigation for prod routes: route horizon14b int4 -> horizon14b int8 for user-facing low-latency endpoints, keep int4 for background/embeds. schedule a canary rollback if eval BLEU < -3.0 vs float16.
Jordan: +1 on fallback route. also consider a KV compaction backport to runtime v1.14 (low-risk). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtimes/pull/4521 (draft)
Ops: if OOMs surface in prod, runbook suggestion:
1) immediately route traffic to int8 variant (via routing policy)
2) scale up instance type to 12xA100 reserved pool for affected customers
3) trigger incident channel and attach canary logs (`/opt/redwood/logs/horizon14b/*.log`), set kv_compaction_interval to 100 via dynamic config
Maya: putting all this into a short playbook and will post PR for runtime compaction param default change. next steps: Reeva to finish quant sweep, Jordan to run latency p95 tests, Sam to prep routing fallback. thanks all :raised_hands:
